Welspun Living reported an EBITDA of INR 2.5bn, higher than JMfe of 1.9bn. EBITDA was up 
~55% QoQ driven by higher profitability  from home textile segment ( EBITDA up ~53% QoQ) 
and flooring segment ( EBITDA up ~107% QoQ).  Consequently, EBITDA margin came in at 
~10.2%, up ~314bps QoQ. Revenue for the quarter came in at INR24.4bn, up ~8% QoQ as 
geopolitical headwinds moderated, with Home Textile revenue up 6.6% QoQ and Flooring 
revenue up ~10% QoQ.  Key takeaways from the concall are a) FY27 revenue growth guidance 
at double -digits with EBITDA margin expected to expand into teens, b)  company targets zero 
net debt by end -FY27 with FY27 capex guided at

cted to expand into teens, b)  company targets zero 
net debt by end -FY27 with FY27 capex guided at INR4 -5bn towards modernisation and 
debottlenecking , and c) Nevada pillow facility has partially commenced operations with utility 
bedding revenues expected to scale from ~USD27mn in FY26 to ~USD60mn in FY27 . Company 
noted discussions are ongoing with customers to share elevated (higher cotton / fuel prices) 
input costs while clarity on tariff refunds awaited . We believe multiple newer markets opening 
on the back of FTAs and GOI ’s focus on developing the textile ecosystem is likely to drive 
earnings trajectory for the company.  Maintain BUY. 
▪ Margins recover amidst a challenging year: Consolidated EBITDA for Welspun Living stood at

ear: Consolidated EBITDA for Welspun Living stood at 
INR2.5bn, higher than JMfe of 1.9bn. EBITDA was up ~55% QoQ driven by higher EBITDA from 
home textile segment ( up ~53% QoQ) and flooring segment ( up ~107% QoQ). Consequently, 
EBITDA margin came in at ~10.2%, up ~314bps QoQ. Revenue for the quarter came in at 
INR24.4bn, up ~8% QoQ given subduing geopolitical headwinds with Home Textile segment 
revenue  up 6.6% QoQ and Flooring revenue (up 10% QoQ). Adjusted PAT came in at INR1bn vs. 
INR192mn in 3QFY26, up significantly QoQ. Net Debt stood at ~INR7.75bn as at end of 4Q vs 
~INR13bn as at end of 3Q. Company incurred a capex of ~INR4.7bn in FY26. Global brands 
contributed ~12% of revenues while Innovation contributed ~22% in FY26.   The company has 
approved buyback of up to ~14mn e

nues while Innovation contributed ~22% in FY26.   The company has 
approved buyback of up to ~14mn equity shares worth ~INR2.5bn at a price of INR175 per share. 
Company has announced dividend 10% per equity share for the FY26. 
▪ Muted performance across segments; domestic business a bright spot: Home textile revenue 
increased QoQ by ~7% to INR23.1bn. The flooring business revenue increased by ~10% QoQ to 
INR1.9bn. Home textile business reported EBITDA of INR 2.4bn with margins at 10.5% during 
4QFY26 vs 7.3% in 3QFY26 as tariff -related customer discounts eased during the quarters . 
Flooring business reported EBITDA of INR 60mn, up significantly by ~ 107% QoQ.  Domestic 
business remained a key lever, growing 29.2% YoY in 4QFY26 and achieving EBITDA breakeven, 
with domestic flooring

ed a key lever, growing 29.2% YoY in 4QFY26 and achieving EBITDA breakeven, 
with domestic flooring up 25.3% YoY. On utilisation, Bath Linen improved 5% QoQ to 79% while 
Bed Linen declined 19% QoQ to 57%, with Rugs & Carpets stable at 75%.  
▪ FTA-led structural tailwinds set the stage for FY27 recovery :  Company guided double-digit 
revenue growth in FY27 with EBITDA margins expected to recover into the teens, backed by 
India's expanding FTA network - India-UK FTA signed Jul'25, India -EU FTA concluded Jan'26, 
and India-US bilateral trade discussions progressing. Non-US markets now contribute ~41% of 
consolidated revenues, providing a meaningful buffer against residual US tariff pressures. 
Company targets zero net debt by end-FY27 (from INR7.8bn currently), with FY27 capex guided

Key Concall Takeaways:  
◼ FY27 Growth Visibility: Management guided for double-digit revenue growth in FY27 backed by 
structural tailw

th Visibility: Management guided for double-digit revenue growth in FY27 backed by 
structural tailwinds, with EBITDA margins expected to expand into the teens. 
◼ Capacity Ramp -Up: Nevada pillow facility has partially commenced operations with utility 
bedding revenue expected to scale from ~USD27mn in FY26 to ~USD60mn in FY27 (~2.2x); Ohio 
pillow facility continue to ramp-up with current utilisation at ~60%. 
◼ Capex & Efficiency:  FY27 capex guided at INR4 -5bn largely towards modernisation and 
debottlenecking; BS strengthening and operational efficiency improvement to continue. 
◼ Christy delivered ~15% growth on strong UK performance; soft flooring remains a high -margin 
segment with 20%+ margin potential. 
◼ Company plans to go to zero net debt by the end of FY27 backed by improv

h 20%+ margin potential. 
◼ Company plans to go to zero net debt by the end of FY27 backed by improving margins and strong 
cash flows. 
◼ Company has cotton inventory cover till October. 
◼ Non-US markets now contribute ~41% of consolidated top -line, providing a meaningful buffer 
against US tariff headwinds. 
◼ 4QFY26 margins were lower YoY on account of lower volumes and higher tariff related discounts; 
management indicated this as a quarter-specific dynamic. 
◼ Discussions ongoing with customers on sharing higher input costs (cotton, fibres, fuel) amid a 
weaker rupee; tariff refund clarity awaited given 80%+ business on FOB basis.
